text:
ops-bot: 🚨 Incident detected: ORD GPU node eviction spike, 2025-06-12 03:12 UTC. High pod churn and degraded inference latency. auto-scale events firing.
maya: Seeing ~40% of GPU pods evicted in the last 5m, queue backlog rising. Triggered dedicated-fallback to 'cpu-shed' pool.
sanjay: Network rate increases from a single customer flow correlated with egress ACL logs around 03:08. Suspect traffic storm causing kubelet memory pressure on nodes.
liam: Confirmed warm-pool empty for ORD. New node boots slower because image pull contention. Warm-pool refill failed at 02:55 due to quota spike.
maya: Latency SLOs violated for realtime route /v1/generate, we've routed ~18% traffic to AMS as temporary failover.
erin: Can we throttle evictions to avoid cascade? Current kube eviction daemon seems too aggressive under transient pressure.
jon: Trying a manual eviction-throttle: set cluster annotation eviction.rate.limit=0.2 to slow eviction loop. Applying now: `kubectl annotate ns infra eviction.rate.limit=0.2`
sanjay: Throttle applied, pods are stabilizing. Backlog decreasing but some nodes still degraded (OOM/kubelet).
liam: Starting warm-pool refill with staggered image prefetch, 5s jitter: `./warmpool-refill --region=ord --count=12 --jitter=5s`
maya: Noted a weird behavior where our failover policy immediately re-routed all traffic when node count dipped 15% — we want a gradual shift. Need playbook change.
erin: Proposed playbook edit: add a sliding shift window: when region degradation <20% shift up to 25% traffic; between 20-50% shift in 10% increments every 2m with verification.
jon: Also add a capacity-hedge pre-provision step: if eviction_rate > 5/min, pre-warm N GPUs (configurable) and notify on-call.
sanjay: Root cause summary for postmortem: noisy egress flow from partner X triggered control-plane API retries -> kubelet memory pressure -> rapid pod eviction -> warm-pool exhaustion -> reactive all-or-nothing failover.
liam: Immediate mitigations we did: 1) eviction throttle annotation 2) staged warm-pool refill 3) partial traffic shift to AMS 4) temporarily increased image-pull concurrency limits on node pools.
maya: Suggest runbook additions (short bullets):
- Add 'eviction-throttle' knob and exact command + rollback steps.
- Sliding traffic-shift heuristic (percent windows + cooldown).
- Warm-pool health probe and auto-refill threshold (e.g., if warm_pool_count < 30% trigger prewarm).
- Egress-flow detection: correlate egress rate to kubelet OOMs and alert.
- Failover partial-rollout command snippets and verification checks.
sanjay: I'll draft the playbook PR. Assigning tasks: @sanjay -> PR for runbook edits, include commands + test checklist. @liam -> automation for warm-pool prefetch with jitter. @maya -> add observability dashboards for eviction_rate and warm_pool_count. @erin -> update failover policy config and add unit tests for sliding-window logic.
jon: Post-incident action items and owners:
- Create runbook PR with exact `kubectl annotate` examples and rollback steps. (sanjay, due EOD)
- Add eviction_rate alert with runbook link and paging (maya, 24h)
- Implement warm-pool auto-refill + test harness (liam, 3d)
- Add egress anomaly detector to infra-alerts (erin, 2d)
- Run tabletop for ORD failover scenario next Tues (ops, schedule)
maya: Quick note: cost impact estimate — shifting ~18% to AMS for 45m increased token cost ~+12% for that window. Add cost guardrails to failover playbook: maximum budgeted cross-region fallback per incident.
erin: Agree. Add a flag `failover_budget_usd` and `max_shift_percent` to the policy.
sanjay: Draft PR link: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/infra-runbooks/pull/428 (WIP)
liam: We'll also add a small canary pre-shift step: route 1% first and monitor for 2m before increasing.
maya: Can we add a non-disruptive test in staging that simulates eviction + warm-pool exhaustion so the sliding shift behavior is validated?
liam: Yes — use the chaos harness: `./chaos-sim --region=ord --scenario=warm-exhaust --duration=10m`
jon: All good. Current status: ORD stabilized, backlog drained, warm-pool at 65% after refill. We'll keep monitoring 2h.
ops-bot: Incident closed for now (stabilized). Log saved to incident-2161234567.
